own_solution.law: Momentum conservation per absorption: N = p_atom / p_photon = sqrt(2 m K) / (h / lambda); spontaneous-emission recoil averages to zero
assumptions: each absorbed photon transfers h/lambda opposite to motion
lambda = 589 nm throughout (sweep negligible for photon momentum)

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T7F35 and T037E say 'a little' instead of stating 0.011 eV, so they differ in the number from their apparent variants T28D1 and T341F/TC3E2.
defect_reasons.other: The 2.4 GHz sweep (T0167/T866E) exceeds the Doppler shift needed to stop one atom (v/lambda = 800 m/s / 589 nm = 1.36 GHz); not a contradiction since one atom need not use the whole sweep, but slightly odd; also TC3E2/TCE76 leave mildly open whether 0.0763 eV already includes the nozzle increment.

notes: p = sqrt(2*3.81924e-26 kg*1.22246e-20 J) = 3.0558e-23 kg m/s; h/lambda = 1.12496e-27 kg m/s; N = 2.7163e4. With 0.0873 eV: N = 27163*sqrt(0.0873/0.0763) = 27163*1.06966 = 2.9056e4. Initial speed ~800 m/s. Scattering rate affects only the slowing time, not N. I read TCE76/TC3E2 as adding 0.011 eV to the stated 0.0763 eV.
